      Seconded By: Paula Fletcher

      Greater Toronto Area (GTA) through the form of a living history

      post-confederation period;
      AND WHEREAS TRCA has undertaken efforts to modernize and
      enhance programming and service offerings at The Village to
      reflect both the diverse history of the GTA from the Indigenous
      pre-colonial era through to the current multicultural metropolis

      AND WHEREAS 2026 Community Museum Operating Grant
      (CMOG) funding requires a board-approved, updated long-term
      strategic or guiding plan;
      THEREFORE LET IT BE RESOLVED THAT TRCA’s 2026-2031

      AND THAT the 2026-2031 Guiding Plan for The Village at Black
      Creek be submitted to the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and
      Gaming as per CMOG funding conditions;

10.1.1    RENAMING TOMMY THOMPSON PARK TO TOMMY
      THOMPSON NATURE RESERVE
      RES.#A 137/26
      Moved By: Linda Jackson
      Seconded By: Paula Fletcher
      WHEREAS Tommy Thompson Park, located on the Leslie Street
      Spit at the Toronto waterfront, is one of Toronto's most
      significant urban natural areas and provides important habitat
      for birds, fish, reptiles, amphibians, mammals and diverse plant
      communities;
      WHEREAS Tommy Thompson Park is designated as an
      Environmentally Significant Area in the City of Toronto Official
      Plan and is recognized internationally as an Important Bird Area
      for its importance to the conservation of birds and their habitat;
      WHEREAS TRCA owns and manages the principal lands
      comprising Tommy Thompson Park, in partnership with the City
      of Toronto and TRCA have worked together for decades to
      protect, restore and provide public access to this unique urban
      wilderness;



                                    15
 WHEREAS the site has evolved from a lake filling and
construction-waste disposal area into a significant urban
wilderness through natural succession, habitat creation,
ecological restoration and long-term stewardship by TRCA, the
City of Toronto, community organizations, volunteers and other
partners;
WHEREAS the City of Toronto and TRCA have established a
joint-management approach for Tommy Thompson Park and the
broader Leslie Street Spit, recognizing the importance of
integrated management of the lands, ecological systems, public
access and visitor experience;
WHEREAS the name "Tommy Thompson" has long been
associated with the site and recognizes the contribution of
Tommy Thompson, Toronto's first Commissioner of Parks, and
in 1984 the Leslie Street Spit was officially named Tommy
Thompson Park in his honour; and
WHEREAS Tommy Thompson's legacy is closely associated
with Toronto's parks system and the development and
stewardship of public green space, and retaining his name in the
proposed name "Tommy Thompson Nature Reserve" recognizes
that history while more clearly reflecting the site's present-day
role as an urban wilderness and significant natural area;
WHEREAS the name "Nature Reserve" more clearly
communicates to residents and visitors the ecological character,
purpose and significance of the site, while retaining the
established and historically significant name "Tommy
Thompson";
WHEREAS a proposal to rename the site "Reserve" was
previously considered in or around 2019 and was not ultimately
implemented, and the proposal provides an opportunity to
revisit that matter in light of the City's and TRCA's subsequent
work on joint management, ecological restoration and the
long-term future of the Leslie Street Spit;
WHEREAS the Community Advisory Group has expressed
support for the proposed name "Tommy Thompson Nature
Reserve";


                            16
 WHEREAS the proposed name would retain the longstanding
Tommy Thompson name while more accurately communicating
the site's character as an urban wilderness and significant
natural area;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT:
The Board of Directors endorse the proposed renaming of
Tommy Thompson Park to "Tommy Thompson Nature Reserve";
TRCA request the General Manager, Parks and Recreation, in
consultation with TRCA, to undertake any necessary
administrative, mapping, wayfinding, signage and
communications changes arising from the approved name
change;
TRCA request the General Manager, Parks and Recreation, in
consultation with TRCA, to review the 2019 report and related
documentation concerning the proposed naming of Tommy
Thompson Park and incorporate any relevant findings or
recommendations into the implementation of the proposed
renaming;
TRCA request that the renaming process include appropriate
consultation with the Tommy Thompson Park community, user
groups, community advisory representatives and other relevant
stakeholders; and
TRCA request the General Manager, Parks and Recreation, to
report back to the appropriate committee on the outcome of the
consultation and coordination.



                                                         Carried

Item 8.9
Section I – Items for Board of Directors Action

TO:        Chair and Members of the Board of Directors
           Friday, November 6, 2026 Meeting
FROM:      Mike Puusa, Associate Director, Restoration and Infrastructure

RE:        VENDORS OF RECORD FOR RENTAL OF OPERATED
           CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT – TERM AND VALUE
           EXTENSION FOR AN ADDITIONAL TWO YEARS PER RFP
           No. 10042420

KEY ISSUE
Authorization to extend the term and increase the value of Contract No.
10042420: Vendors of Record (VOR) for Rental of Operated Construction
Equipment for an additional two years in accordance with the provisions of
the original contract and vendor agreements.
RECOMMENDATION:

WHEREAS Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) is
engaged in a variety of programs/projects that require operated
construction equipment;
WHEREAS Dynex Construction Inc., Sartor Environmental Group Inc.,
TMI Contracting & Equipment Rental Ltd. and Valefield Contracting
Inc (“Vendors of Record”) were the successful Proponents for the
Request for Proposal (RFP) Contract No. 10042420 for Operated
Construction Equipment;
WHEREAS at its meeting of February 21, 2025, the Board of Directors
approved Resolution #A14/25 establishing a Vendors of Record
arrangement for the period of April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2027, in the
amount of $33,177,500.00, plus applicable taxes, with the option to
extend the arrangement for an additional two (2) one (1) year terms;
WHEREAS the executed agreements with the Vendors of Record
provide for a single two (2) year extension term from April 1, 2027, to
March 31, 2029;
THEREFORE, LET IT BE RESOLVED THAT Resolution #A14/25 be
amended to revise the extension provisions of the Vendors of Record
arrangements from two (2) one (1) year extension terms to a single
two (2) year extension term, consistent with the executed Vendor
                                                                   Item 8.9
agreements;
AND FURTHER THAT TRCA staff be authorized to exercise their
option to extend the VOR arrangement from April 1, 2027, to March 31,
2029, and increase the contract value by $35,700,000, plus applicable
taxes, for a total revised contract value of $68,877,500, plus applicable
taxes; to be expended as authorized by TRCA staff, subject to annual
budget approvals;
AND FURTHER THAT authorized TRCA officials be directed to take
whatever action may be required to implement these extensions,
including the obtaining of necessary approvals and the signing and
execution of any documents.

BACKGROUND
TRCA requires operated construction equipment rentals for completing a
variety of engineering, habitat restoration, and trail building projects
throughout TRCA’s jurisdiction. By establishing a VOR arrangement for
rental of operated equipment, vendors are authorized to provide these
services for a defined period of time and with fixed pricing.

This VOR arrangement provides access to a variety of operated
construction equipment, including but not limited to:

     Bulldozers;                              Rollers;
     Front End Loaders;                       Screeners;
     Excavators;                              Grinders/Chippers; and
     Rock Trucks;                             Skidsteers.
     Dump Trucks;

The VOR supports the delivery of a broad range of capital and
maintenance projects across TRCA's jurisdiction, including bank, slope and
channel stabilization works, shoreline protection projects, habitat
enhancement and restoration initiatives, flood protection works, trail
development projects, and other infrastructure construction and protection
projects.

The initial term of the VOR arrangement is scheduled to expire on March
31, 2027. Subject to the amendment described above, this report seeks
authorization to exercise the two (2) year extension term provided for in the
                                                                   Item 8.9
Vendor agreements, and to approve the additional funding required to
support the extended contract term.

In consultation with TRCA’s Corporate Sustainability group, requirements
for vendors to provide fuel consumption metrics, including fuel tickets, have
been added to this VOR. This requirement will play a crucial role in
developing metrics to track TRCA contractors' greenhouse gas (GHG)
emissions and will support TRCA’s broader initiatives for fleet
decarbonization and GHG reduction.

Additional requirements have been incorporated into this VOR to ensure
that vendors' equipment fleets are updated in compliance with engine

Item 8.2
Section I – Items for Board of Directors Action

TO:           Chair and Members of the Board of Directors
              Friday, November 6, 2026 Meeting
FROM:         Sameer Dhalla, Director, Development and Engineering
              Services

RE:           UPDATE AND APPROVALS FOR THE HIGHLAND
              CREEK MARKHAM BRANCH (CORPORATE DRIVE)
              FLOOD REMEDIATION CLASS ENVIRONMENTAL
              ASSESSMENT
KEY ISSUE
Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) staff are seeking
approval for TRCA to enter into an agreement with the City of Toronto to
provide services and contract administration required to complete the
remaining components of the Highland Creek Markham Branch (Corporate
Drive) Flood Remediation Class Environmental Assessment (EA). Staff are
also seeking approval to authorize additional funding for Stantec to support
completion of the EA.
RECOMMENDATION:

IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT the Update and Approvals for the
Highland Creek Markham Branch (Corporate Drive) Flood
Remediation Class Environmental Assessment report be received;
WHEREAS Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) is
engaged in a project that requires engineering consulting services;
AND WHEREAS TRCA solicited proposals through a publicly
advertised process and evaluated the proposals based on pre-
established RFP criteria and awarded Request for Proposal (RFP)
No.10009966 for Highland Creek Markham Branch (Corporate Drive)
Flood Remediation Class Environmental Assessment to Morrison
Hershfield Limited at a total cost of $412,667.50, plus applicable
taxes;

AND WHEREAS additional scope of work is required to complete the
project which exceeds the previously authorized budget;

AND WHEREAS the City of Toronto has authorized the execution of
                                                                    Item 8.2
the additional scope of work, is committed to completing the project
and committed to paying for the additional expenses;

THEREFORE LET IT BE RESOLVED THAT TRCA enter into an
agreement with the City of Toronto, pursuant to the Master Service
Agreement dated August 15, 2018, to undertake work related to the
Highland Creek Markham Branch (Corporate Drive) Flood
Remediation Class Environmental Assessment, at a total cost not to
exceed $739,361.98, plus applicable taxes, inclusive of consultant
fees, TRCA staff costs, contingency, and related project expenses;

AND THEREFORE LET IT BE RESOLVED THAT a Change Order for
Request for Proposal (RFP) No.10009966 for Highland Creek Markham
Branch (Corporate Drive) Flood Remediation Class Environmental
Assessment be awarded to Stantec (previously Morrison Hershfield
Limited) at a total cost not to exceed $368,215.98, plus applicable
taxes, to be expended as authorized by TRCA staff;
AND FURTHER THAT authorized TRCA officials be directed to take
whatever action may be required to implement the contract, including
the obtaining of necessary approvals and the signing and execution
of any documents.

BACKGROUND
The southeast corner of Corporate Drive and Consilium Place in
Scarborough Centre is owned by 8104476 Canada Inc. (Owner). The
property and surrounding lands are located within the regional flood plain of
the Markham Branch of Highland Creek and form part of the broader
Progress Business Park Flood Vulnerable Area.
In July 2018, Toronto City Council directed TRCA to undertake a Flood
Remediation Study, in consultation with City staff and at the Owner's
expense, to investigate measures to contain the flood plain and support
redevelopment opportunities. TRCA subsequently entered into an
agreement with the Owner and the City of Toronto to complete the study,
consisting of a Technical Study and a Municipal Class Environmental
Assessment (EA). The Owner provided $800,000 to fund consultant fees,
TRCA staff costs, contingency, legal, and other project-related expenses.
The study area experiences flooding during storm events greater than the
25-year storm as a result of flow restrictions at undersized culverts located
at Corporate Drive, Progress Avenue, and Bellamy Road. During these
                                                                    Item 8.2
events, water overtops Corporate Drive and spills onto adjacent lands.
The project is evaluating alternatives to provide flood protection along an
approximately 1.8-kilometre section of the Markham Branch of Highland
Creek. Due to the scale and complexity of the project, a multidisciplinary
engineering team is required to address hydraulic, ecological,
geomorphological, transportation, geotechnical, and environmental
planning considerations. The project is being completed in accordance with
the Municipal Class Environmental Assessment (MCEA) process.
The project was undertaken in two phases:
Phase 1: Technical Study (completed December 2020)
The Technical Study evaluated flood remediation alternatives,
characterized existing conditions, identified potential impacts and mitigation
measures, established feasibility, and confirmed the appropriate EA
process.
Phase 2: Municipal Class EA (initiated 2022)
The Schedule C Municipal Class EA progressed through Phases 1 and 2,
including public and stakeholder consultation, and advanced into Phase 3.
The project was placed on hold in 2023 due to project-related challenges
and remains incomplete.
At Executive Committee Meeting held on May 29, 2019, Resolution
#B67/19 was approved as follows:
      WHEREAS Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) is
      engaged in a project that requires engineering consulting services;

      AND WHEREAS TRCA solicited proposals through a publicly
      advertised process and evaluated the proposals based on pre-
      established RFP criteria;

      THEREFORE LET IT BE RESOLVED THAT Request for Proposal
      (RFP) No.10009966 for Highland Creek Markham Branch (Corporate
      Drive) Flood Remediation Class Environmental Assessment be
      awarded to Morrison Hershfield Limited at a total cost not to exceed
      $299,007.50, plus applicable taxes, to be expended as authorized by
      TRCA staff;

      THAT TRCA staff be authorized to approve additional expenditures to
      a maximum of $68,150.50, plus applicable taxes in the event that the
      Technical Study determines the Municipal Engineers Class
                                                                    Item 8.2
      Environmental Assessment process should be completed as a
      Schedule C project;

      THAT TRCA staff be authorized to approve a contingency for the
      project to a maximum of $55,000 (approximately 15% of the total
      maximum cost), plus applicable taxes, if deemed necessary;

      AND FURTHER THAT authorized TRCA officials be directed to take
      whatever action may be required to implement the contract, including
      the obtaining of necessary approvals and the signing and execution
      of any documents.

RATIONALE
Approval is required for TRCA to enter into an updated agreement with the
City of Toronto to provide services and contract administration for
completion of the Highland Creek Markham Branch (Corporate Drive)
Flood Remediation Municipal Class Environmental Assessment (MCEA).
As portions of the MCEA remain outstanding and the MCEA process has
since been amended, a new agreement is needed to define and address
the remaining scope, roles, responsibilities, and funding required to
complete the project.

Approval is also requested to authorize additional funding for Stantec to
complete the MCEA. Following its acquisition of Morrison Hershfield,
Stantec retains ownership of the existing draft EA documentation and
maintains project-specific knowledge through staff who previously worked
on the project. Continuing with Stantec will support an efficient completion
of the MCEA and provide the best value for TRCA and the City.

Relationship to TRCA’s 2023-2034 Strategic Plan
This report supports the following Pillar(s) and Outcome(s) set forth in
TRCA’s 2023-2034 Strategic Plan:

Pillar 1 Environmental Protection and Hazard Management:
        1.1 Deliver provincially mandated services pertaining to flood and
            erosion hazards
Pillar 1 Environmental Protection and Hazard Management:
        1.4 Balance development and growth to protect the natural
            environment ensuring safe sustainable development
                                                                   Item 8.2

Pillar 2 Knowledge Economy:
        2.4 Integrate environmental considerations and science into
            decision making

FINANCIAL DETAILS
TRCA will enter into a Letter Agreement with the City of Toronto for certain
work and services to be performed by TRCA in connection with the
Highland Creek Markham Branch (Corporate Drive) Flood Remediation
Municipal Class Environmental Assessment (“Project”) pursuant to the
Master Service Agreement dated August 15, 2018 between TRCA and the
City. At the point in time $42,637.84 of budget remains from the earlier
funding agreement between TRCA, the City and the owner of the proposed
redevelopment site within the study area. The City will cover all other costs
associated with the study including Consultant fees, TRCA staff costs,
contingency and other fees related to undertaking the study. Funds for the
contract will be tracked in account 107-65 Highland Creek at Markham
Branch (Corporate Drive) Flood Remediation Study.

DETAILS OF WORK TO BE DONE
The project will include the following key components:

  1. Update to Baseline Inventory

     Baseline conditions include existing physical, biological, cultural,
     socioeconomic, flooding and erosion characteristics. The consultant
     will update certain baseline conditions due to the lapse in time or
     change in study requirements, as determined to be appropriate by
     TRCA and the City.

  2. Update to Evaluation of Alternative Solutions

     The consultant will work with the City of Toronto and TRCA to review
     and update the evaluation criteria and relative weighting of criteria to
     be used for the updated evaluation matrix. Based on this analysis, the
     consultant will assess the outcomes of the evaluation process and
     what mitigating measures are recommended for any adverse
     impacts. The preferred alternative solution will then be confirmed.
                                                               Item 8.2
3. Implementation Phasing Plan

  As requested by the Executive Steering Committee, Stantec and
  GPRA will prepare an implementation phasing plan for the
  construction of flood relief measures and associated erosion
  protection and any other critical phasing consideration. The
  implementation plan will have three phases – one for each proposed
  reconstructed water crossing. The consultants will include modelling,
  flood mapping and construction cost estimates for phasing analysis.

4. Consultation with Public, First Nations and other Stakeholders

  Prior to a public event, meetings with stakeholders, property owners
  and indigenous communities will be held to discuss the revised
  alternative solution evaluation, updated preferred solution as well as
  the implementation phasing plan.

  One public event is required to present the outcome of the evaluation
  of alternative solutions, the preferred solution and proposed phasing
  for implementation. The public event will also provide an explanation
  of the transition of the project from a Schedule C MCEA to a
  Schedule B MCEA and other details of the EA process with respect to
  the revocation of the MCEA that comes into effect in January 2027.

5. Conclusion of the MCEA

  The technical work, MCEA process and findings will be documented
  in an EA File Study Report, to be produced by the consultant and
  reviewed by TRCA and the City. The EA File Study Report will be
  posted for public review and TRCA will distribute a Notice of
  Completion. TRCA and Stantec will coordinate tracking of comments
  during the 30-day review period. Should any Section 16 Order
  request be made, Stantec will support the TRCA in addressing the
  request.

6. Provisional: Pre-Design Report

  Technical work was completed to develop design concepts beyond
  requirements of the current Schedule B MCEA process when this EA
  was classified as a Schedule C. As a provisional item Stantec will
                                                             Item 8.2
     document analysis completed to date beyond Schedule B MCEA
     requirements. This document will serve as a high-level charter
     document to guide a future detailed design of the preferred
     alternative, such as design constraints, detailed modelling,
     correspondence, and recommendations for next steps in the design
     process.

Management

transactions audited annually by a licensed public accountant. The annual
audit provides independent assurance over TRCA's financial statements
and supports accountability and transparency in the management of public
funds and other financial resources.

The audited financial statements are presented to the Board of Directors
and, as required under the Act, provided to participating municipalities and
the Province and made publicly available. The external audit process also
provides an opportunity to identify financial reporting issues, internal control
weaknesses and areas for improvement.

TRCA's external audit arrangements also include the annual audits of the
Toronto and Region Conservation Foundation's financial statements and
The Village at Black Creek's statement of revenue and expenditures. The
Foundation is a separate legal entity and is responsible for approving its
own auditor appointment and funding its audit costs.

KPMG LLP has served as TRCA's external auditor. On August 28, 2026,
KPMG provided formal notice that it would no longer be providing external
audit services to TRCA. As a result, TRCA initiated a competitive
procurement process to appoint a new external auditor beginning with the
2026 fiscal year-end.

The RFP was issued for an initial two-year term, with an option to renew for

KEY ISSUE
Award of Request for Tender (RFT) No #10045110 for erosion control,

RECOMMENDATION:
WHEREAS Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) is
engaged in a project that requires a General Contractor to implement
the East Highland Creek Erosion Control Project following completion
of detailed design in 2025;
AND WHEREAS TRCA solicited tenders through a publicly advertised
process with submissions evaluated based on pricing received from
five (5) pre-qualified Bidders selected through a previously completed
Request for Pre-qualification (RFPQ) process.
THEREFORE, LET IT BE RESOLVED THAT RFT No. 10045110 for the
implementation of erosion control, slope stabilization, and
infrastructure construction works at East Highland Creek near
Ellesmere Road be awarded to 614128 Ontario Ltd. o/a Trisan
Construction, at a total cost not to exceed $761,536.00 plus applicable

AND FURTHER THAT authorized TRCA officials be directed to take

of any documents.

BACKGROUND
Section 5 of The Meadoway Multi-use Trail is located near Ellesmere Road,
between Military Trail and Neilson Road, within the East Highland Creek
ravine landscape. Ongoing channel migration and erosion within Highland
Creek have resulted in deterioration of adjacent armourstone retaining
walls and retreat of the valley slope toward newly constructed Meadoway
trail infrastructure.

In 2022, as part of the Section 5 works, TRCA constructed a pedestrian-
cycling bridge over East Highland Creek, an elevated boardwalk, and
connecting multi-use trails to enhance active transportation connectivity
while minimizing environmental impacts. The project area is located
adjacent to an unstable valley wall affected by erosion, steep slopes, and
ongoing hydraulic forces. Given its proximity to a Provincially Significant
Wetland and sensitive valley corridor habitats, any required stabilization
measures must be carefully designed to address slope instability while
limiting impacts on the surrounding natural environment.

Interim erosion control measures were implemented during construction of
this section of The Meadoway in 2022 to temporarily reduce risks to the
bridge, boardwalk, trail infrastructure, and surrounding ecological features.

Subsequent technical investigations confirmed that these measures are not
sufficient as a long-term solution. The studies identified continued channel
migration, bank erosion, over-steepened slopes, and hydraulic forces as
key drivers posing a risk to the long-term integrity of the bridge, boardwalk,
and trail network and requires permanent intervention.

The East Highland Creek Erosion Control Project has therefore been
established to provide long-term stabilization of the creek and valley
corridor, protect Meadoway infrastructure, maintain safe and reliable trail
access, and address ongoing erosion processes within the site. TRCA
                                                                    Item 8.11
retained Aquafor Beech Ltd. in late 2023 through a competitive process to
advance the detailed design, which was finalized in 2025.

The design includes coordination and integration with future channel
stabilization and sanitary sewer protection initiatives planned by the City of
Toronto within Highland Creek to support broader long-term objectives for
infrastructure resilience, watershed management, and valley corridor
stability.
